# Pyrox — HYROX race results data

> Pyrox makes HYROX race results available as structured data. It's an
> independent, MIT-licensed open-source project, not affiliated with or endorsed
> by HYROX. Two access paths: a Python package (`pyrox-client`) that returns
> races as pandas DataFrames, and a public, read-only MCP server that lets AI
> assistants answer questions about HYROX results directly.

## Access points

- MCP endpoint (public, read-only, no authentication, rate-limited):
  `https://pyrox-api.fly.dev/mcp/`
- Python package: `pip install pyrox-client`
- Source: https://github.com/vmatei2/pyrox-client
- Docs: https://vmatei2.github.io/pyrox-client/

## MCP tools

- `list_filters`: available seasons, divisions, genders, locations, age groups
- `list_races`: valid season and location pairs
- `find_athlete`: resolve an athlete name to candidate results (`result_id`)
- `get_race_report`: one result's full race, split by split
- `get_athlete_profile`: historical results and personal bests
- `get_distribution`: histogram bins and summary stats for a cohort
- `get_race_summary`: timing stats for every segment in one race
- `get_cohort_segment_averages`: run/station averages for all, top-N, bottom-N
- `get_rankings`: leaderboard rows and hypothetical target-time placement
- `get_deepdive`: one result against cross-location cohorts for a metric

All tools are read-only and idempotent. The server computes analytics; it
doesn't expose arbitrary SQL or bulk row exports.

## Vocabulary

- **Race**: one HYROX event instance (season, location, year)
- **Result**: one athlete's performance in one Race
- **Segment**: one timed Run or Station
- **Roxzone**: transition time between Segments
- **Cohort**: the reference population for rankings, distributions, percentiles
- **Distribution**: histogram bins plus summary stats for a metric in a cohort

Divisions are `open`, `pro`, `doubles`, `pro_doubles`, `relay`, `adaptive`.
Pyrox doesn't pool them by default because they aren't directly comparable.
Seasons, locations and age groups change with the dataset, so discover them with
`list_filters` rather than assuming.

## Example questions it can answer

- Where would a 62-minute male open time rank in season 8?
- Show the distribution of female open finish times in season 8.
- Summarise this athlete's race report and name their strongest segment.
- How do the top 10% of finishers split their runs versus the field?

## Docs

- [MCP server guide](https://vmatei2.github.io/pyrox-client/mcp/): install steps
  for Claude Code, Claude web/Desktop and Codex, full tool list, example prompts
- [Quickstart](https://vmatei2.github.io/pyrox-client/quickstart/): Python setup

- [Data model](https://vmatei2.github.io/pyrox-client/data-model/): columns and units
- [Filtering](https://vmatei2.github.io/pyrox-client/filters/): query options
- [Analytics](https://vmatei2.github.io/pyrox-client/analytics/): worked recipes
- [FAQ](https://vmatei2.github.io/pyrox-client/faq/)

## Caveats

Pyrox is built on public HYROX source data and may inherit issues present in it.
Thin cohorts come back flagged with sample-size information, and distributions
default to the latest season and the `open` division when those filters are
omitted.
